explanations: C-1. Compared with no Kestland Household Support Payment Act 2027, compliance cost for households.no_account rises from the short run onward (tier A, invisible). Why: CR-8: every payment is a receipt: what one side no longer pays or receives is what the other keeps or loses. This holds if: no assumption. Reported.

C-2. Compared with no Kestland Household Support Payment Act 2027, enforcement cost for officials.enforcement rises from the short run onward (tier A, invisible). Why: OC-3: the measure must be administered, and a raised budget is paid for by taxpayers. This holds if: no assumption. Reported.

C-3. Compared with no Kestland Household Support Payment Act 2027, resources available other uses for taxpayers.later or public_spending_recipients.later falls for at least one of them from the medium run onward (tier A, invisible). Why: SB-1: a subsidy is paid by someone: taxes now, or borrowing repaid from taxes later; OC-1: what the payers give up is what they would otherwise have bought. This holds if: no assumption. Reported.

source_sentences: Households resident in Kestland on 1 April 2027 receive 1,000 crowns per household, once, tax-free, not counted as income for benefits.
The Tax Agency pays by direct deposit from 1 July 2027 to the 3.4 million households with bank details on file.
Others apply by form, with identity documents, by 31 December 2027, and are paid within eight weeks.
The Finance Minister announced the payment in the budget speech on 4 March 2027.
The Tax Agency runs payment runs, application processing, a call center and identity checks.
False claims must be repaid, with a fine of 2,000 crowns, and may be prosecuted as fraud.
The administration is funded from the borrowing.
The principal and interest on the bonds are repaid from general revenue in ten equal annual installments from 2028.

context: Government debt is about 45% of the yearly product, and the government sells about 35 billion crowns of bonds in a typical year; about 30% of its bonds are held abroad.
About 35% of households report less than one month's income in liquid savings.
A survey of intentions by Kestland Statistics in March 2027 found that 30% of households planned to save most of the payment, 40% to pay bills or debts, and 30% to spend it on goods and services.
A 2014 energy rebate of 300 crowns per household was followed by higher card spending in the following two months.
record.name: Kestland Household Support Payment Act 2027

readings: U1-a: one payment per registered address
U1-b: one payment per tax-filing unit, so the payments due (about 4.6 million) exceed the borrowing of 4.1 billion crowns
unclear.text: What a household is: one payment per registered address, or one per tax-filing unit.
How the later installments are funded: higher taxes, lower spending, or both.
